newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds up with Bunds, seen drifting.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds up with Bunds, seen drifting.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds stepped smartly higher on the coattails of German Bunds on Monday after a four-day break, but traders said there was no real interest in the market and they expected it to drift.
"Bunds opened higher and we went with them. But there is no activity. It is very very quiet," one trader said.
Traders said the OLO exchange auction on Tuesday when players will get the last opportunity to swap out of OLO 15 was weighing on prices but not necessarily activity.
There is just below 100 billion Belgian francs still outstanding in the issue.

Traders discounted talk of rising tensions between the country's French and Dutch speaking communities in the run up to decision day early next year on countries judged fit to join European Economic and Monetary Union.

"It is true that because of EMU and the savings we have had to make a lot of problems have cropped up again. But tensions between the two communities seem to emerge every spring and then fade away again," one trader said.
"It is all to do with money. I don't see this government falling -- at least not until after the EMU decision is taken sometime around next spring," the trader added.
Traders said the focus of attention in coming days would be U.S. April producer prices due at 1230 GMT on Wednesday, and the expected publication of German tax receipt figures.
At 0900 GMT the yield of the benchmark 2007 OLO was 5.85 percent against Wednesday's closing 5.87, and the spread over Bunds was 11 basis points against 10.
The June futures contract was 17 basis points higher at 121.44.
